parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
You can read a great novel, listen to a great symphony, or go to see a painting by a great artist, and you'll want to experience it again and again. And every time you do, you'll learn something new from it.

Very few films achieve this. Most of them are mere entertainment, and very few of them could be said to be works of art. They simply don't have the depth that a work of art has, and this means that you may see them once, but you won't want to watch them again.

Why is it that so many commercial films today have such a limited shelf life? One problem is that for many films, once you've seen them once and you know what happens, that's it. They rely on the element of surprise to keep you interested, and once that's lost, that feeling of what's going to happen next, there's nothing left.

In addition, the commercial nature of filmmaking means that rather than focusing on the development of characters in the film, many films are just becoming vehicles for actors. Box office successes who essentially play the same part each time. Then, as well as this, many critics would argue that the greatest black and white films had their own special world with its own special atmosphere, and that nowadays it's harder to create this because the director is unable to play with light in the same way.

Another problem is that many directors lack the ability to focus the camera on the important points. There may be impressive visual images, but they don't contribute to the meaning of the film.

Which brings me on to Ingmar Bergman, the great Swedish film director who died in 2007. No other director has equaled Bergman in his ability to convey Emotion. His films have the dramatic force of a work by the world's greatest playwrights such as Ibsen or Shakespeare.

Watching Bergman's films is an enriching experience. Nothing is immediately obvious or predictable, but gradually it becomes clear where he is taking you. If you study a film such as Wild Strawberries, you'll see that every little detail is significant. Each image on the screen is there for a purpose and gradually builds up an understanding of the central meaning.

With Bergman too, you know that a small gesture made by a character or the expression on a character's face can tell you just as much as the Words uttered. In his film Persona, the central character says nothing, but meaning is conveyed by what we see on the screen.

But Bergman wasn't just a great cinematographer, he was also a great storyteller. Each of his films follows a similar pattern in that the story is organized on two levels. Firstly, on the level of a straightforward, dramatic narrative, but secondly, on the level of myth, and the story works throughout the film on both these levels.

In Bergman's film Wild Strawberries, an old man travels back to the places he knew as a child and a young man. In the film, we can identify themes that occur again and again in Bergman's work. First of all, we have the idea of the journey. Part of the journey is a real one, but linked with that is the theme of Dreams where they can take us and what we can learn from them.

Another theme, which was to be central to Bergman's work throughout his life, is that of relationships, and in particular, the ties that join the members of a Family together. And finally, as the old man in Wild Strawberries struggles to make sense of his life, we have another theme which underlies all his work. No matter how anxious or unhappy his characters may appear to be, and that is that we have to Accept everything that life can give. It's not a fashionable philosophy, and it may be why Bergman's films have fallen out of fashion. But in...

analyses.content: 录音提到大多数电影只是娱乐，缺乏艺术品所拥有的“深度”（depth）。

Most of them are mere entertainment, and very few of them could be said to be works of art. They simply don't have the depth that a work of art has, and this means that you may see them once, but you won't want to watch them again.
你可能会听到“works of art”，但空格前有 the，需要填入艺术所具备的特质名词。

In addition, the commercial nature of filmmaking means that rather than focusing on the development of characters in the film, many films are just becoming vehicles for actors. Box office successes who essentially play the same part each time.
录音里提到了“vehicles（工具/载体）”，但题目问的是依赖的对象，即具体的“actors”。
商业电影不再关注角色发展，而是变成了票房成功的“演员”（actors）的工具。
影评人认为现在的导演无法像以前那样通过操纵“光线”（light）来营造特殊的氛围。
...and that nowadays it's harder to create this because the director is unable to play with light in the same way.
No other director has equaled Bergman in his ability to convey Emotion. His films have the dramatic force of a work by the world's greatest playwrights such as Ibsen or Shakespeare.
题目中的 portray 对应录音中的 convey，听到这个动词后紧跟的名词就是答案。
伯格曼拥有一种独特的能力，能够传达/描绘“情感”（emotion）。

If you study a film such as Wild Strawberries, you'll see that every little detail is significant. Each image on the screen is there for a purpose and gradually builds up an understanding of the central meaning.
录音里先说了每一个细节都很 significant（重要），但后面紧跟的 is there for a purpose 才是填空的核心。
录音明确指出，银幕上的每一个画面都有其“目的”（purpose）。
一个小动作或面部表情传达的信息和说出来的“话语”（words）一样多。
With Bergman too, you know that a small gesture made by a character or the expression on a character's face can tell you just as much as the Words uttered.
录音中用了 uttered（说出）来修饰 words，填空时只需要提取核心名词词汇。

Each of his films follows a similar pattern in that the story is organized on two levels. Firstly, on the level of a straightforward, dramatic narrative, but secondly, on the level of myth, and the story works throughout the film on both these levels.
录音中先说了 narrative（叙事），听到 but secondly（第二个层面）之后出现的词就是 myth。
他的故事在两个层面展开：一个是戏剧叙事，另一个是“神话”（myth）层面。
Part of the journey is a real one, but linked with that is the theme of Dreams where they can take us and what we can learn from them.
题目问的是旅程和什么的 connection（联系），录音用 linked with（连接）引出了 dreams。
在电影《野草莓》中，现实的旅程与“梦境”（dreams）的主题紧密相连。
Another theme, which was to be central to Bergman's work throughout his life, is that of relationships, and in particular, the ties that join the members of a Family together.
录音提到 relationships，但题目空格在 relationships 前面，需要填入修饰语 family。
伯格曼作品的另一个核心主题是人际关系，尤其是“家庭”（family）成员之间的纽带。
...we have another theme which underlies all his work. No matter how anxious or unhappy his characters may appear to be, and that is that we have to Accept everything that life can give.
听到 underlying theme（潜在主题）后，注意谓语动词 have to 后面跟着的动作就是 accept。
电影传达的思想是：无论生活给予什么，我们都必须“接受”（accept）。
